newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah stable, swaps ease in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah stable, swaps ease in late trade.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was stable against the dollar in slow late trading on Wednesday, with swap rates edging down on offshore selling, dealers said.
One local bank dealer said offshore operators who went long over the past two days were squeezed with expensive swap rates, forcing them to unload spot dollars and swaps.
Spot rupiah was quoted at 2,323.20/23.50 at 0900 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,326.5/27.0.
Dealers said the downtrend in dollars and swap premiums had started since early trading.
They said fresh economic data announced on Wednesday was positive for the rupiah but did not affect the market much.

Indonesia's consumer price index declined 0.04 percent month-on-month in September, compared with a rise of 0.27 percent in August. It posted a trade surplus of $508.5 million in July against $193.4 million in June.
"Operators who had gone long could not withstand the high swap rates anymore. They have to liquidate it," the local bank dealer said, adding that swap rates had stabilised for now.
Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,322.5/23.0 and 2,323.25/23.75, respectively.
The dealer said some operators were also seen anticipating possible tighter liquidity conditions this Friday.
"It's quite usual that some players open short positions on a Wednesday to speculate on a tight rupiah supply on Friday. They can cash out at the weekend," he said.
Dealers said liquidity had been tight in the past three Fridays, with short-dated swap rates soaring to as high as three points.
"There was some kind of psychological impact in the market. It might not be tight, but people are not expecting ample supply (on that day)," the local bank dealer said.
He said the downtrend in inflation did not necessarily mean a decline in interest rates in the domestic market.
The dealer said interest rates remained firm and an easing was not anticipated in the near term due to fierce competition for deposits in the domestic market.
Overnight swap was at 0.55/0.65 and tom/next at 0.55/0.60.
One-month swap was at 17.5/18.0, two at 33.0/34.5, three at 51.5/52.5 and six at 99.5/100.0 points.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention rate by one point to 2,317/2,509 and the conversion rate also by one point to 2,317/2,365 on Wednesday. -- Jakarta newsroom +6221 384-6364.
